slides.heading: f-Strings
slides.body: f-Strings is part of Mathematical and String Operations. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: f-Strings
slides.body: An f-string lets you insert variable values directly into text using braces. It makes messages easier to format.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: An f-string is like a certificate template where the name is filled into a blank space.

annotations.note: This line stores or updates a value using a variable.
This line displays a value or message on the screen.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Python follows operator rules exactly. Use variables and parentheses to make calculations readable and predictable.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Use an f-string to print Hi, followed by the value of name.

quiz.prompt_text: Which of the following correctly uses an f-string to insert a variable into text?
quiz.explanation: Correct! In an f-string, variables must be inside curly braces {}. print(f"Hello, {name}") inserts the value of name directly into the string.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines in the correct order to greet a user by name using an f-string.
quiz.explanation: The comment comes first, then the variable is assigned, and finally the f-string uses the variable to build and display the greeting.

quiz.prompt_text: Use an f-string to print a greeting that includes the name stored in the variable name.
quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: print(f"Hi, {name}") outputs "Hi, Luna". The f before the quote enables the f-string, and {name} is replaced with the variable's actual value.
